items.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023
items.q: Makoto used to say to me, he said, “You know why we play so well together?” ... In fact Makoto and I toured around for about three years because of that record we made.

ctx.x: A guy comes into your office and you say, “Well let’s play a tune.” And you know pretty much where he’s at when within about 30 seconds. And you can recognize budding talent at all levels. I mean the level is huge. So once you’ve — I mean there’s the one who hasn’t a musical bone in his or her body but there are those and you kind of gently try to aim them in another direction. Then you have Makoto Ozone and Kirill Gerstein coming in at the age of twelve and you go oh my God is that unbelievable. And then you try…

Have you had experiences as time went on when some students might have come from really well established jazz programs in high school or perhaps they had teachers, and they would come to you and ask you about techniques or theory that was either foreign to you or that you didn’t necessarily believe in, but they wanted to know about it?
